properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued November 19 at 9:09PM EST until November 19 at 11:15PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
FFWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Eastern Indian River County in east central Florida...

* Until 1115 PM EST.

* At 909 PM EST, emergency management reported flooding is occurring
on multiple roadways in Sebastian. Up to 1.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.5 inches are possible
in the warned area over the next hour and a half. Flash flooding is
already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Sebastian, Vero Beach, Fellsmere, Indian River Shores, Wabasso,
Sebastian Highlands, Winter Beach, Gifford, Roseland, Vero Beach
South, Sebastian Inlet, Vero Lake Estates, Pointe West, Sebastian
Inlet State Park, Orchid, Vero Beach Airport, Wabasso Beach,
Disneys Vero Beach Resort and North Beach.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb through Minor Flood
Stage at the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through this weekend. Towards late weekend and into
early next week, the river is anticipated to reach Major Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 4.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Thursday was 4.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 5.7 feet early next
week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:37PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Above Lake Harney near Geneva affecting Seminole
County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is occurring and Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The forecast river level is above the all time flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River Above Lake Harney near Geneva.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 10.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Thursday was 10.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.0 feet
this weekend.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:29PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage, and it
has already exceeded record flood stage. Additional heavy rainfall
over the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above
record flood levels through late week and into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The forecast river level is above the all time flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 18.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Thursday was 18.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage, cresting at 18.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:24PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due
to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination
with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 3.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Thursday was 3.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Tuesday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 17 at 8:21AM MST until November 24 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues.

* WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with
flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately
downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet.
- Flooding is expected along the Gila River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
